purpose: Canonical project-interpretive North/West/East/South orientation profiles for the World Map. These are versioned relational readings, not sovereignty, consent, annexation, legal command or institutional membership.

north.label: North
north.summary: Canada–North Atlantic–Nordic–European strategic field extending through Central Europe, the Baltic, eastern Europe and the Balkans toward Ukraine and Türkiye.

west.label: West
west.summary: US/Israel-centered project field with the wider American system and strong Atlantic/Pacific overlaps.

east.label: East
east.summary: China/Russia/India-centered Eurasian field with BRICS/SCO correspondence but no implied ideological unity.

south.label: South
south.summary: Polycentric Australian/Blue-Pacific, Antarctic and Southern African/Indian Ocean field; intentionally not the whole Southern Hemisphere.

orientations.note: Recovered Canada-to-Türkiye North formulation begins with Canada.
Canada remains deeply connected to the American and Atlantic security/economic system.
Denmark/Kingdom context is a recurrent North anchor in project language.
Iceland is repeatedly part of the North Atlantic/North chain.
Norway is a recurrent Nordic/North Atlantic North node.
Sweden is explicitly part of the Scandinavian North field.
Finland is explicitly part of the recovered North field.

Estonia was explicitly described as under/within the North Axis field.

Latvia completes the Baltic segment of the project North field between the Nordic/Baltic anchors and the eastern European corridor. This is a project interpretation, not a sovereignty or alliance claim.

Lithuania completes the Baltic segment of the project North field and connects the Nordic/Baltic system toward Poland and Ukraine. This is a project interpretation, not a sovereignty or alliance claim.
Poland is treated as a principal continental hinge in the project North field between Germany/Baltic Europe and Ukraine. This project role is distinct from NATO, EU or other empirical memberships.
Romania extends the project North field along the eastern European and Black Sea corridor toward Ukraine and Türkiye. This is an interpretive overlap, not a formal-bloc claim.
Czechia is included as a continental North connector within the Germany–Poland–eastern European capability corridor. Its project role is not derived automatically from institutional membership.
Slovakia is included as a continental North connector between central Europe, Poland and the Ukraine-facing eastern corridor. This is project interpretation rather than institutional classification.

Switzerland is included as a Central European bridge inside the project North geography while retaining its distinct neutrality and institutional position. This is a project interpretation, not an alliance claim.

Austria is included as a Central European connector linking Germany, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia and the wider continental North corridor. This is project interpretation, not institutional classification.
Slovenia extends the Central European North corridor toward the Adriatic and western Balkans. This project role does not imply a separate legal or military bloc.
Hungary is represented as a North bridge because it lies inside the Central/Eastern European corridor while maintaining a more complex set of east-west political and economic relationships.
Croatia extends the project North corridor from Central Europe into the Adriatic and western Balkans. This is a project interpretation distinct from formal institutional membership.
Serbia is represented as a bridge within the Balkan North corridor because its geography and relationships connect European and wider Eurasian systems. This does not imply alliance alignment.
Montenegro is included in the Adriatic/Balkan extension of the project North field. The classification is project-geographic rather than a sovereignty or hierarchy claim.
Albania is included in the Adriatic/Balkan extension of the project North field, linking the western Balkans toward Greece and the wider Mediterranean corridor.
Bulgaria extends the project North corridor through southeastern Europe toward the Black Sea, Greece and Türkiye. This remains an interpretive project classification.
North Macedonia is included as a Balkan connector between Serbia, Albania, Bulgaria and Greece inside the project North corridor.
Moldova is included in the eastern European North corridor between Romania and Ukraine. This is a project-geographic classification, not a formal alliance claim.

Bosnia and Herzegovina is included to keep the western Balkan North corridor geographically coherent between Croatia, Serbia and Montenegro. This is project interpretation, not institutional classification.
Ukraine is explicitly a later strategic extension of North.
Türkiye is the late endpoint/gate in the recovered Canada-to-Türkiye formulation.
Türkiye also connects Europe to Black Sea, Caucasus, Middle Eastern and SCO-adjacent systems.
England/UK is strongly West-linked in recovered project language.
The memorable North formulation was Canada-to-Türkiye minus England; later UK language remained variable rather than fully excluded from northern systems.
